title: pgvector
subtitle: Vector search inside PostgreSQL backs the memory service's hybrid retrieval and the capabilities model's data factory.

stats.label: dimensions declared on the memory vector column, checked at the boundary

lede: In the memory capability of FAFOHive I wanted one query to search by meaning, match exact identifiers and filter by project, so I kept vectors in PostgreSQL with pgvector, in the same row as the text and metadata they describe. Retrieval, filtering and audit are then one query. Each observation, a decision or fix captured from a coding session, carries an embedding beside a weighted full-text column, provenance fields and token-savings accounting. The weighted full text catches exact identifiers that embeddings blur. Embeddings come from a the multilingual embedding model model on a local embedding server. The code index stores chunk embeddings the same way, partitioned per index so I can add or drop one cleanly.
quote: For me pgvector is a decision about where vectors belong.
evidence: Vector search and ANN indexes: pgvector embeddings in the same PostgreSQL row as text, metadata and provenance, so meaning, exact identifiers and project filters are one query.
Hybrid retrieval: weighted full-text and dense rankings fused and reranked by a cross-encoder, with fusion alone as the fallback when the reranker is saturated.
Type-safe data access: a resolver that reads a vector column's declared dimension from its type modifier, binding 1,024-value embeddings and refusing any other length.
author: Corey James
